elements.quote: This systematic review followed Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020 guidelines.
elements.reason: The abstract explicitly describes the work as a systematic review.

elements.quote: This review synthesizes global evidence on challenges, opportunities and strategic directions for embedding OH within health system structures.
elements.reason: The abstract states the main objective of synthesizing evidence on challenges, opportunities, and strategic directions for embedding One Health.

elements.quote: Peer-reviewed studies published between 1 June 2013, and 1 April 2025 were identified through searches conducted in January-February 2025 in Scopus, PubMed, Web of Science and ProQuest Health and Medicine. ... Two reviewers independently screened studies and applied predefined eligibility criteria.
elements.reason: The abstract provides partial inclusion criteria (peer-reviewed studies and date range) but does not explicitly report the main inclusion and exclusion criteria.

elements.quote: Peer-reviewed studies published between 1 June 2013, and 1 April 2025 were identified through searches conducted in January-February 2025 in Scopus, PubMed, Web of Science and ProQuest Health and Medicine. Supplementary searches included Google Scholar and backward reference screening.
elements.reason: The abstract identifies information sources (databases plus supplementary searches) and reports when the searches were conducted (January–February 2025).
The abstract does not specify methods used to assess risk of bias.

elements.quote: Findings were synthesized narratively.
elements.reason: The abstract reports the result synthesis method (narrative synthesis).

elements.quote: Results: Of 2606 records identified, 17 studies were included. The studies represented Africa, Europe, Asia, Australia and multicountry settings across varying income levels.
elements.reason: The abstract provides the total number of included studies and summarizes relevant characteristics (regions/settings), but it does not report included participants.

elements.quote: Key challenges included weak governance arrangements, limited legal and policy support, inadequate financing, workforce capacity constraints and persistent sectoral fragmentation. Opportunities were linked to heightened awareness of zoonotic threats and antimicrobial resistance, growing institutional endorsement, academic engagement and emerging multisectoral coordination mechanisms.
elements.reason: The abstract reports results for main outcomes/themes (challenges and opportunities) but does not provide outcome-specific numbers of studies and participants.

elements.quote: Study Design: A systematic review with narrative synthesis.
elements.reason: The abstract indicates narrative synthesis and does not report any meta-analysis summary estimate or confidence/credible interval.

elements.quote: Findings were synthesized narratively.
elements.reason: No group comparisons and no direction of effect are described in the abstract.
The abstract does not briefly summarize limitations of the included evidence (e.g., risk of bias, inconsistency, imprecision).

elements.quote: Conclusion: Sustainable integration of OH requires embedding it within governance, financing and service delivery systems rather than implementing it as parallel initiatives.
elements.reason: The abstract provides a general interpretation with implications for sustainable integration.
The abstract does not specify the primary source of funding for the review.
The abstract does not provide the register name and registration number.

elements.quote:
Despite its significance, OH remains largely unintegrated into national governance and service delivery structures, with limited coordination across human health, animal health and environmental sectors [ 14 ], and only a few countries demonstrating uneven progress toward cross-sectoral integration [ 16 ].
...
As a result, there remains limited clarity on how governance arrangements, financing mechanisms, workforce capacity and institutional coordination collectively influence the integration of OH into national health systems.
elements.reason: Describes gaps/uncertainties in existing knowledge (limited clarity on how key health-system functions collectively influence OH integration).

elements.quote:
Despite its significance, OH remains largely unintegrated into national governance and service delivery structures, with limited coordination across human health, animal health and environmental sectors [ 14 ], and only a few countries demonstrating uneven progress toward cross-sectoral integration [ 16 ].
...
Accordingly, this systematic review synthesizes global evidence on the challenges and opportunities of integrating OH into national health systems across human, animal and environmental sectors and identifies actionable system-level strategies to support sustainable integration.
elements.reason: Explains why the review is needed by highlighting the lack of integration/coordination and stating that the review will synthesize evidence and identify strategies.

elements.quote:
More recent reviews published in 2025 [ 30-32 ] have examined operational challenges in rural African contexts, ethical considerations within a globalized OH framework and critical reflections from the Global South. Although these contributions broaden thematic and regional understanding, they primarily focus on conceptual or context-specific dimensions rather than systematically analysing how implementation barriers and facilitators intersect with core health system functions.

As a result, there remains limited clarity on how governance arrangements, financing mechanisms, workforce capacity and institutional coordination collectively influence the integration of OH into national health systems.

A comparative synthesis is therefore necessary to identify recurring structural barriers and enabling factors across diverse contexts.
elements.reason: Cites other (recent) reviews and explains why a new review is required based on limitations of those prior reviews.

The retrieved evidence does not describe an intervention effects review or a proposed mechanism of action for an intervention; the review is described as synthesizing implementation challenges/opportunities for integrating One Health.

The retrieved evidence does not present a logic model to hypothesise relationships between intervention components and outcomes; the focus is on integration challenges/opportunities and system-level strategies rather than a logic-modelled intervention.

elements.quote: This review synthesizes global evidence on challenges, opportunities and strategic directions for embedding OH within health system structures.
elements.reason: An objective/aim is stated (to synthesize evidence on challenges, opportunities and strategic directions), but the evidence does not show that objectives or questions are explicitly formulated using a relevant question-formulation framework.

elements.quote: Study Design: A systematic review with narrative synthesis.
elements.reason: The review is described as a narrative synthesis, not as an intervention effects review requiring planned comparisons using PICO (and no such comparisons are described in the retrieved evidence).

elements.quote: Eligibility criteria were structured using the PICo framework (population, interest and context), which is appropriate for non-clinical and policy-focused research questions: Population (P) : national health systems, institutions and stakeholders involved in OH implementation. Interest (I) : challenges, opportunities, barriers, facilitators and implementation strategies related to OH integration. Context (Co) : human, animal and environmental health sectors at national or sub-national levels.
elements.reason: The review specifies PICo-based eligibility components (population, interest, context), but does not explicitly specify eligible study characteristics such as eligible study designs, settings, and any follow-up requirements within the eligibility criteria.

elements.quote: This review includes peer-reviewed studies published between 1 June 2013, and 1 April 2025... Only peer-reviewed journal articles published in English were included. Conference abstracts lacking full-text availability were excluded... Grey literature was also excluded to ensure methodological consistency and comparability across included studies.
elements.reason: The dissemination characteristics are specified, including publication date range, language (English), and publication/report status (peer-reviewed journal articles; exclusions for conference abstracts without full text and for grey literature).
The evidence does not state a distinction between exclusions because outcomes were not measured versus because outcome results were not reported.
The evidence provided describes narrative/thematic synthesis, but does not specify groups used in each synthesis or link them to comparisons defined in the review objectives.

elements.quote: Conference abstracts lacking full-text availability were excluded due to insufficient methodological detail, empirical findings or policy-relevant analysis required to extract implementation challenges, opportunities or recommendations. Grey literature was also excluded to ensure methodological consistency and comparability across included studies.
elements.reason: Rationales are provided for notable eligibility restrictions (exclusion of conference abstracts without full text and exclusion of grey literature).

The retrieved evidence identifies databases and reports that strategies/date ranges are provided in Supporting Information S2, but it does not report the date when each information source was last searched or consulted.

elements.quote: Studies were identified through online database searches... The search was conducted in Scopus, PubMed, Web of Science and ProQuest Health and Medicine... The complete search strategies for each database, including Boolean operators and database-specific adaptations, are provided in Supporting Information S2 .
elements.reason: Database names are reported, and it is stated that complete database-specific strategies (including date ranges/filters) are in Supporting Information S2; however, the retrieved evidence does not provide the coverage dates and interface/platform details for each database in the main text.
No study registers, regulatory databases, or online repositories are described in the retrieved evidence.

elements.quote: Additionally, Google Scholar was used as a supplementary search tool to identify relevant studies that may not be indexed in traditional bibliographic databases.
elements.reason: The online source name (Google Scholar) is reported, but the URL is not provided in the retrieved evidence.
The evidence states the search strategy was reviewed in consultation with a professional health librarian, but no organisations/manufacturers contacted are named.

elements.quote: The search strategy was developed in consultation with and reviewed by a professional health librarian to enhance methodological rigour and completeness. Corresponding authors of any literature identified were not contacted for additional information.
elements.reason: The types of individuals involved (professional health librarian; corresponding authors not contacted) are described.

elements.quote: Following full-text screening, the reference lists of all included studies were manually reviewed to identify additional eligible articles.
elements.reason: The review includes manually reviewing reference lists of all included studies (i.e., the type of reference lists examined is specified).

elements.quote: Full-text assessment and backward citation tracking were conducted to minimize this risk; however, expanded citation network analysis in future reviews may further reduce the possibility of omission.
elements.reason: Backward citation tracking is mentioned, but the seed reports/citation index or platform and the search date are not reported in the retrieved evidence.
No journals or conference proceedings consulted are reported in the retrieved evidence.

elements.quote: The complete search strategies for each database, including Boolean operators and database-specific adaptations, are provided in Supporting Information S2 .
elements.reason: The manuscript states that full, database-specific search strategies (with Boolean operators and adaptations) are provided for each database in Supporting Information S2.
